<addendum>
# Repository: IDX Financial Report Pipeline (`financial-report-llm`)

This project downloads financial reports from the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX),
converts them to markdown (docling), parses XLSX statements into DuckDB, and runs a
multi-stage LLM analysis pipeline that writes equity-research notes into the
`analysis/` Obsidian vault.

## Layout

- `scripts/report_pipeline/` — download → identify → collect → convert + XLSX parser
- `scripts/analysis_pipeline/` — 6-stage LLM analysis pipeline (needs `OPENCODE_API_KEY`)
- `scripts/notes_rag/rag.py` — hybrid BM25 + vector search over `analysis/`
- `idx_data/pipeline.duckdb` — pipeline state + financial data (source of truth)
- `idx_data/notes_rag.duckdb` — vault search index
- `raw/` identified PDFs · `results/` converted markdown · `analysis/` Obsidian vault

## Environment

- Python dependencies live in `.venv`; run scripts as `.venv/bin/python <script>` or
  `uv run <script>`.
- `duckdb` CLI is installed. Open the database read-only:
  `duckdb -readonly idx_data/pipeline.duckdb`.
- Model IDs and timeouts live in `config.yaml`; secrets (`OPENCODE_API_KEY`,
  `EXA_API_KEY`) in `.env` (gitignored — never commit or print).
- `.pi/settings.json` declares the project's pinned pi packages
  (`npm:pi-exa-search@0.1.3`, `npm:pi-web-access@0.41.0`) plus a delta entry
  that disables the global `npm:pi-web-search` extensions in this project.
  Project packages load after project trust (`--approve` for pipeline runs).
- Stage 3b (research) runs on pi with `exa_search` / `fetch_content`; Stage 4
  (writer) also runs on pi but with the read-only idx-tools `duckdb_query`,
  `notes_search`, `notes_fetch` plus `read`.
- `.pi/xdg/pi/web-search.json` configures `pi-web-access` for the Stage 3b
  research runner (fed via `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`); `.agents/skills/` holds dev-time
  Agent Skills (e.g. `build-with-exa`), not loaded by research runs.

## Conventions

- Quote financial values with their units, source table, and period.
  `financial_ratios` values are in billions of IDR (except `eps`);
  `xlsx_statements` values are raw IDR.
- Period formats: `financial_ratios.period` is `"YYYY-MM-DD"`; `xlsx_statements.period`
  and `pipeline_jobs.period` are lowercase `audit | tw1 | tw2 | tw3`.
- Prefer the notes vault (`notes_search`) and DuckDB (`duckdb_query`) over guessing.
  Cite the note path or the table you queried.
- Never commit runtime artifacts: `.env`, `idx_data/analysis/`, `.venv`, `idx_data/*.duckdb`.

## Project skills (`.pi/skills/`)

- `idx-financial-db` — query company ratios, balance sheet, income statement, cash flow
- `vault-search` — search the `analysis/` equity-research notes
- `report-review` — review/write an IDX equity analysis
- `data-pipelines` — run/inspect the report and analysis pipelines

</addendum>

# PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (ITMG) — Q2 2026
---

**Basis of preparation:** This analysis covers the six-month period ended 30 June 2026 ("6M26"), compared against the six months ended 30 June 2025 ("6M25") for income-statement and cash-flow items and against 31 December 2025 ("FYE25") for balance-sheet items. All figures are in **thousands of US Dollars** unless otherwise stated, drawn from the unaudited interim consolidated financial statements (source XLSX, authorised for issue 10 August 2026). Audited status: not stated for the interim (audited: null — treat as unaudited). Reported statement of cash flows and P&L are for the full six-month period; the quarter "Q2 2026" label reflects the interim filing cadence. Prior-period comparatives in the fact sheet for cash flow are 6M25. Reporting currency: USD; closing rate Rp17,856/US$ (30 Jun 2026) vs Rp16,782/US$ (31 Dec 2025); average rates Rp17,196 (6M26) vs Rp16,475 (6M25).

## 1. Executive Summary

ITMG delivered a solid first half: net revenue of US$1,000,491k (+8.8% YoY from US$919,416k), gross profit of US$256,477k (+14.1%), and net profit of US$109,514k (+16.5%), lifting net margin to 10.9% from 10.2%. Gross margin expanded ~2pp to 25.6% on an approximately +5% volume / +4% ASP mix (management-reported 12.3 Mt sold vs 11.7 Mt; ASP ~$81/t vs ~$78/t per ITMG's 6M26 news release, 10 Aug 2026), with own-coal sales up 11% while lower-margin third-party trading fell 20%. The external backdrop was supportive: high-kcal ESDM HBA benchmarks climbed through Q2 (US$123.91–131.85/t for 6,322 kcal/kg GAR across June–July periods) and Newcastle futures spiked to ~US$150/t in early June before easing, while Indonesia's RKAB quota cuts and DMO obligations tightened supply.

The balance sheet remains a fortress: cash of US$737,575k (plus US$66,442k short-term deposits per Note 9) against total bank debt of only US$18,360k net carrying value (Note 35 financing reconciliation), a current ratio of 3.46x, working capital of US$843,582k, and equity of US$1,910,488k (79.1% of assets). Two balance-sheet shifts deserve attention: restricted cash jumped 77% to US$85,787k, driven by the switch of mine reclamation/post-mining guarantees from bank guarantees to time deposits under Kepmen ESDM 344/2025 (all reclamation bank guarantees have been withdrawn and replaced with time deposits per the commitments note) — structurally "dead money"; and current prepaid taxes nearly doubled to US$55,677k as Indonesia's tax-refund (restitusi) pipeline slowed sharply (DJP refunds down ~33–38% YoY through 2026), a medium-confidence external explanation. The same refund slowdown is the primary driver of the 77.8% collapse in operating cash flow to US$62,376k (management: tax refund receipts ~US$169m lower YoY).

Capital returns are accelerating: 21,186,800 shares (1.9% of capital) repurchased in H1 for Rp464.5bn (US$26,571k), plus a further 10,690,300 shares (0.9%) in the subsequent-events window for Rp256.1bn (US$14,341k), under a mandate capped at Rp2,490bn; FY2025 dividends of US$114,584k (US$0.10/share full-year) were paid across the period. Annualized ROE of ~22.9% and ROA of ~18.2% on an exceptionally unlevered book make the earnings quality high even in a mediocre coal tape. No market data stub was provided, so valuation multiples are not computable here and are flagged as not available; the one comparable in the pipeline DB (ADRO, Oct-2025: P/E 5.65x, P/BV 0.62x, ROE 10.9%) suggests the sector continues to trade at deep-value multiples. Net thesis: a high-quality, net-cash thermal coal producer compounding shareholder returns through buybacks in a cyclical price environment with rising regulatory cash entanglement. The rating leans **HOLD/BUY on weakness** pending coal-price confirmation — see §14.

## 2. Revenue Analysis

### 2.1 Revenue Performance

| Metric | 6M26 (US$'000) | 6M25 (US$'000) | % Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Net revenue | 1,000,491 | 919,416 | +8.8% |
| Coal — third parties | 963,940 | 897,155 | +7.4% |
| Coal — related parties | 36,758 | 10,772 | +241% |
| Services | 1,626 | 2,257 | −28.0% |
| (Loss)/gain on coal swap | (1,833) | 9,232 | n.m. |

(Note 24 composition; percentages computed on the fact-sheet lines.) Revenue growth of 8.8% is volume- and price-led rather than trading-led. Related-party coal sales (Banpu entities, 3.67% of net revenue vs 1.17% in 6M25) rose sharply but remain immaterial to mix. The coal-swap line flipped from a US$9,232k gain to a US$1,833k loss, a ~US$11.1m earnings swing worth understanding: ITMG operates a volume-based swap programme (max 8,000,000 tonnes, tenors up to three years per Note 34) that flattens realised prices against index moves.

### 2.2 Revenue Drivers — Volume vs. Price

Per ITMG's own 6M26 news release (itmg.co.id, 10 Aug 2026 — external, management-disclosed figures): sales volume +5% to 12.3 Mt (11.7 Mt in 6M25) and ASP +4% to ~US$81/t (~US$78/t). Within that, own-coal sales rose 11% to 10.5 Mt while third-party trading fell 20% to 1.8 Mt — a favourable mix shift toward higher-margin own production. The same release flags production down 5% YoY to 9.9 Mt and a strip ratio of 10.3x (vs 9.3x), meaning the volume gain was partly inventory/trading-flow driven.

Price environment: ESDM HBA for 6,322 kcal/kg GAR printed US$123.91/t (period I June), US$126.58/t and US$131.85/t (periods I–II July 2026) per Bisnis.com (17 Jul 2026); Newcastle futures spiked to ~US$150/t in early June on Middle East conflict, then eased ~18% to a ~US$125–138/t range through July (CNBC Indonesia, 28 Jun 2026). Indonesia's 2026 RKAB quota cuts and DMO obligations constrained supply, supporting ASP. FX was a modest headwind on Rupiah cost translation (average Rp17,196 vs Rp16,475) but revenue is USD-denominated.

### 2.3 Revenue Composition Observations

Geographic mix (Note 34 / segment disclosures, 6M26 vs 6M25, US$'000): China 270,701 vs 243,211 (+11%); Japan 268,691 vs 203,860 (+32%); Philippines 104,432 vs 44,007 (+137%); Thailand 41,658 vs 10,772 (+287%); India 39,051 vs 115,100 (−66%); Domestic 174,660 vs 205,497 (−15%); Hong Kong 26,666 vs 23,071; Malaysia 21,886 vs 0 (new); Taiwan 16,712 vs 15,445; Vietnam 14,950 vs 0 (new); Bangladesh 14,423 vs 28,137 (−49%); Korea 6,661 vs 14,507 (−54%); Europe 0 vs 15,809. This matches the regional trade pattern: Asia's thermal imports rebounded (73.16 Mt in July, Reuters 28 Jul 2026) while India's seaborne thermal imports hit a four-year low on domestic output and renewables (Reuters, 18 Jun 2026). Customer concentration: three customers each owed >US$10,000k, equal to 43.65% of trade receivables (FYE25: four customers, 40.56%); Marubeni Corporation is disclosed as a >10%-of-net-revenue third-party customer in both periods (receivable balances US$135,384k at 30 Jun 2026 vs US$83,618k at 30 Jun 2025). Related-party receivables rose to 9% of trade receivables from 0%.

### 2.4 Revenue Sustainability and Forward Outlook

Key watch items: (1) post-period coal prices eased into a "lukewarm" tape by August (CNBC Indonesia, 2 Aug 2026) — H2 ASPs may not repeat Q2's spike; (2) Government Regulation No. 24/2026 (effective 1 June 2026) requires progressive channelling of coal, palm oil and ferro-alloy exports through BUMN Ekspor with a transition period ending 31 December 2026 — a structural change to export marketing not yet quantified by management; (3) MoEMR No. 6/2026 adds prior-approval requirements for coal blending and quarterly reporting — management assessed no material impact as at 30 June 2026; (4) DHE SDA rules (GR 8/2025, amended by 2/2026 and 21/2026) require export proceeds to sit in special accounts ≥12 months, with monthly conversion capped at 50% — already visible in the US$56,570k of DHE SDA special accounts and time deposits inside cash; (5) royalty audits at TCM for FY2018–2023 are in progress (letters received 12 May 2026). Reserve/runway: production and reserve tables were not disclosed in this chunk — cannot be stated. Permit runway is solid (BEK CCoW to 2041, TCM to 2035, JBG to 2035; see §7.2), but IMM's CCoW expires 31 March 2028, the nearest meaningful permit cliff.

## 3. Profitability Analysis

### 3.1 Gross Margin Analysis

| Metric | 6M26 (US$'000) | 6M25 (US$'000) | % / bps Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 1,000,491 | 919,416 | +8.8% |
| COGS | 744,014 | 694,704 | +7.1% |
| Gross Profit | 256,477 | 224,712 | +14.1% |
| Gross Margin | 25.64% | 24.44% | +120 bps |

COGS detail (Note 25): mining costs US$385,426k, royalty US$110,939k, coal purchases US$106,456k (down from US$143,964k — consistent with the 20% drop in third-party trading volume). Supplier concentration: PT Pamapersada Nusantara alone is >10% of net revenue at US$318,115k (6M25: US$259,748k), up 23% YoY — the contract-mining cost lever moved against ITMG more than revenue did. Despite a strip ratio rising to 10.3x (vs 9.3x) and sector cost inflation of 10–15% cited by APBI, gross margin expanded 120 bps, evidencing pricing power. External caution (Aldiracita 2Q26 flash, medium-high confidence): 2Q26 gross margin compressed ~2.1pp QoQ to ~24.6% even while up ~4.1pp YoY — the H1 YoY gain is partly off a weak 2Q25 base, with 2Q26 cash cost ex-royalty/depreciation estimated at ~US$60.2/t (+9.2% QoQ).

### 3.2 Operating Margin Analysis

The statements do not present a separate operating-profit caption; the computed operating-margin ratio is null. The implied derivation from fact-sheet lines (gross profit less selling less G&A):

| Metric | 6M26 (US$'000) | 6M25 (US$'000) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Gross Profit | 256,477 | 224,712 |
| Selling expenses | (88,197) | (81,162) |
| G&A expenses | (26,033) | (18,652) |
| Implied operating profit (derived) | 142,247 | 124,898 |
| Implied operating margin (derived) | 14.2% | 13.6% |

Selling expense rose 8.7%, broadly in line with revenue; embedded in it is a marketing service fee to ultimate parent Banpu of US$11,768k (13.34% of selling expenses, vs US$8,996k / 11.08% in 6M25). G&A jumped 39.7% (others component to US$14,295k from US$7,477k); no explanation is disclosed — flagged as an open item (see §11.4 and internal_must_explain). External research (low confidence) suggests a step-up from 1Q26 rather than a 2Q26 event, possibly treasury-programme/transformation costs — treat as hypothesis only.

### 3.3 Net Finance Income/Expense and Other Income

- Finance income: US$18,046k (bank interest US$18,013k + other interest US$33k) vs US$20,569k in 6M25 — lower despite the rate environment, reflecting shrinking deposit balances (short-term deposits fell to US$66,442k from US$141,095k).
- Finance costs: US$3,719k vs US$5,501k (−32.4%), with loan interest nil (6M25: US$2,140k) consistent with the Rp320.2bn (US$17,931k) repayment of the Permata term loan during the half; residual costs are lease-related (Note 11: lease interest US$2,594k).
- Others, net: swung to −US$2,137k embedded net effect of an FX gain of US$6,414k (6M25: loss US$939k) offset by other losses of US$4,277k (6M25: US$1,644k). The fact-sheet caption records other_income_net of −US$4,277k. The composition (FX vs swap MTM vs disposals) is per Note 29 context: derivative liabilities rose to US$5,642k from US$278k at FYE25. The rupiah weakened ~6.1% over the half (average Rp17,196 vs Rp16,475), yet an FX gain was booked — the Note 33 swing of net Rupiah monetary position from net liabilities (US$20,335k) to net assets (US$6,906k) supports this; treat exact drivers as unresolved.

**Basis of preparation:** This analysis covers the six-month period ended 30 June 2026 ("6M26"), compared against the six months ended 30 June 2025 ("6M25") for income-statement and cash-flow items and against 31 December 2025 ("FYE25") for balance-sheet items. All figures are in **thousands of US Dollars** unless otherwise stated, drawn from the unaudited interim consolidated financial statements (source XLSX, authorised for issue 10 August 2026). Audited status: not stated for the interim (audited: null — treat as unaudited). Reported statement of cash flows and P&L are for the full six-month period; the quarter "Q2 2026" label reflects the interim filing cadence. Prior-period comparatives in the fact sheet for cash flow are 6M25. Reporting currency: USD; closing rate Rp17,856/US$ (30 Jun 2026) vs Rp16,782/US$ (31 Dec 2025); average rates Rp17,196 (6M26) vs Rp16,475 (6M25).

## 1. Executive Summary

ITMG delivered a solid first half: net revenue of US$1,000,491k (+8.8% YoY from US$919,416k), gross profit of US$256,477k (+14.1%), and net profit of US$109,514k (+16.5%), lifting net margin to 10.9% from 10.2%. Gross margin expanded ~2pp to 25.6% on an approximately +5% volume / +4% ASP mix (management-reported 12.3 Mt sold vs 11.7 Mt; ASP ~$81/t vs ~$78/t per ITMG's 6M26 news release, 10 Aug 2026), with own-coal sales up 11% while lower-margin third-party trading fell 20%. The external backdrop was supportive: high-kcal ESDM HBA benchmarks climbed through Q2 (US$123.91–131.85/t for 6,322 kcal/kg GAR across June–July periods) and Newcastle futures spiked to ~US$150/t in early June before easing, while Indonesia's RKAB quota cuts and DMO obligations tightened supply.

The balance sheet remains a fortress: cash of US$737,575k (plus US$66,442k short-term deposits per Note 9) against total bank debt of only US$18,360k net carrying value (Note 35 financing reconciliation), a current ratio of 3.46x, working capital of US$843,582k, and equity of US$1,910,488k (79.1% of assets). Two balance-sheet shifts deserve attention: restricted cash jumped 77% to US$85,787k, driven by the switch of mine reclamation/post-mining guarantees from bank guarantees to time deposits under Kepmen ESDM 344/2025 (all reclamation bank guarantees have been withdrawn and replaced with time deposits per the commitments note) — structurally "dead money"; and current prepaid taxes nearly doubled to US$55,677k as Indonesia's tax-refund (restitusi) pipeline slowed sharply (DJP refunds down ~33–38% YoY through 2026), a medium-confidence external explanation. The same refund slowdown is the primary driver of the 77.8% collapse in operating cash flow to US$62,376k (management: tax refund receipts ~US$169m lower YoY).

Capital returns are accelerating: 21,186,800 shares (1.9% of capital) repurchased in H1 for Rp464.5bn (US$26,571k), plus a further 10,690,300 shares (0.9%) in the subsequent-events window for Rp256.1bn (US$14,341k), under a mandate capped at Rp2,490bn; FY2025 dividends of US$114,584k (US$0.10/share full-year) were paid across the period. Annualized ROE of ~22.9% and ROA of ~18.2% on an exceptionally unlevered book make the earnings quality high even in a mediocre coal tape. No market data stub was provided, so valuation multiples are not computable here and are flagged as not available; the one comparable in the pipeline DB (ADRO, Oct-2025: P/E 5.65x, P/BV 0.62x, ROE 10.9%) suggests the sector continues to trade at deep-value multiples. Net thesis: a high-quality, net-cash thermal coal producer compounding shareholder returns through buybacks in a cyclical price environment with rising regulatory cash entanglement. The rating leans **HOLD/BUY on weakness** pending coal-price confirmation — see §14.

## 2. Revenue Analysis

### 2.1 Revenue Performance

| Metric | 6M26 (US$'000) | 6M25 (US$'000) | % Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Net revenue | 1,000,491 | 919,416 | +8.8% |
| Coal — third parties | 963,940 | 897,155 | +7.4% |
| Coal — related parties | 36,758 | 10,772 | +241% |
| Services | 1,626 | 2,257 | −28.0% |
| (Loss)/gain on coal swap | (1,833) | 9,232 | n.m. |

(Note 24 composition; percentages computed on the fact-sheet lines.) Revenue growth of 8.8% is volume- and price-led rather than trading-led. Related-party coal sales (Banpu entities, 3.67% of net revenue vs 1.17% in 6M25) rose sharply but remain immaterial to mix. The coal-swap line flipped from a US$9,232k gain to a US$1,833k loss, a ~US$11.1m earnings swing worth understanding: ITMG operates a volume-based swap programme (max 8,000,000 tonnes, tenors up to three years per Note 34) that flattens realised prices against index moves.

### 2.2 Revenue Drivers — Volume vs. Price

Per ITMG's own 6M26 news release (itmg.co.id, 10 Aug 2026 — external, management-disclosed figures): sales volume +5% to 12.3 Mt (11.7 Mt in 6M25) and ASP +4% to ~US$81/t (~US$78/t). Within that, own-coal sales rose 11% to 10.5 Mt while third-party trading fell 20% to 1.8 Mt — a favourable mix shift toward higher-margin own production. The same release flags production down 5% YoY to 9.9 Mt and a strip ratio of 10.3x (vs 9.3x), meaning the volume gain was partly inventory/trading-flow driven.

Price environment: ESDM HBA for 6,322 kcal/kg GAR printed US$123.91/t (period I June), US$126.58/t and US$131.85/t (periods I–II July 2026) per Bisnis.com (17 Jul 2026); Newcastle futures spiked to ~US$150/t in early June on Middle East conflict, then eased ~18% to a ~US$125–138/t range through July (CNBC Indonesia, 28 Jun 2026). Indonesia's 2026 RKAB quota cuts and DMO obligations constrained supply, supporting ASP. FX was a modest headwind on Rupiah cost translation (average Rp17,196 vs Rp16,475) but revenue is USD-denominated.

### 2.3 Revenue Composition Observations

Geographic mix (Note 34 / segment disclosures, 6M26 vs 6M25, US$'000): China 270,701 vs 243,211 (+11%); Japan 268,691 vs 203,860 (+32%); Philippines 104,432 vs 44,007 (+137%); Thailand 41,658 vs 10,772 (+287%); India 39,051 vs 115,100 (−66%); Domestic 174,660 vs 205,497 (−15%); Hong Kong 26,666 vs 23,071; Malaysia 21,886 vs 0 (new); Taiwan 16,712 vs 15,445; Vietnam 14,950 vs 0 (new); Bangladesh 14,423 vs 28,137 (−49%); Korea 6,661 vs 14,507 (−54%); Europe 0 vs 15,809. This matches the regional trade pattern: Asia's thermal imports rebounded (73.16 Mt in July, Reuters 28 Jul 2026) while India's seaborne thermal imports hit a four-year low on domestic output and renewables (Reuters, 18 Jun 2026). Customer concentration: three customers each owed >US$10,000k, equal to 43.65% of trade receivables (FYE25: four customers, 40.56%); Marubeni Corporation is disclosed as a >10%-of-net-revenue third-party customer in both periods (receivable balances US$135,384k at 30 Jun 2026 vs US$83,618k at 30 Jun 2025). Related-party receivables rose to 9% of trade receivables from 0%.

### 2.4 Revenue Sustainability and Forward Outlook

Key watch items: (1) post-period coal prices eased into a "lukewarm" tape by August (CNBC Indonesia, 2 Aug 2026) — H2 ASPs may not repeat Q2's spike; (2) Government Regulation No. 24/2026 (effective 1 June 2026) requires progressive channelling of coal, palm oil and ferro-alloy exports through BUMN Ekspor with a transition period ending 31 December 2026 — a structural change to export marketing not yet quantified by management; (3) MoEMR No. 6/2026 adds prior-approval requirements for coal blending and quarterly reporting — management assessed no material impact as at 30 June 2026; (4) DHE SDA rules (GR 8/2025, amended by 2/2026 and 21/2026) require export proceeds to sit in special accounts ≥12 months, with monthly conversion capped at 50% — already visible in the US$56,570k of DHE SDA special accounts and time deposits inside cash; (5) royalty audits at TCM for FY2018–2023 are in progress (letters received 12 May 2026). Reserve/runway: production and reserve tables were not disclosed in this chunk — cannot be stated. Permit runway is solid (BEK CCoW to 2041, TCM to 2035, JBG to 2035; see §7.2), but IMM's CCoW expires 31 March 2028, the nearest meaningful permit cliff.

## 3. Profitability Analysis

### 3.1 Gross Margin Analysis

| Metric | 6M26 (US$'000) | 6M25 (US$'000) | % / bps Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 1,000,491 | 919,416 | +8.8% |
| COGS | 744,014 | 694,704 | +7.1% |
| Gross Profit | 256,477 | 224,712 | +14.1% |
| Gross Margin | 25.64% | 24.44% | +120 bps |

COGS detail (Note 25): mining costs US$385,426k, royalty US$110,939k, coal purchases US$106,456k (down from US$143,964k — consistent with the 20% drop in third-party trading volume). Supplier concentration: PT Pamapersada Nusantara alone is >10% of net revenue at US$318,115k (6M25: US$259,748k), up 23% YoY — the contract-mining cost lever moved against ITMG more than revenue did. Despite a strip ratio rising to 10.3x (vs 9.3x) and sector cost inflation of 10–15% cited by APBI, gross margin expanded 120 bps, evidencing pricing power. External caution (Aldiracita 2Q26 flash, medium-high confidence): 2Q26 gross margin compressed ~2.1pp QoQ to ~24.6% even while up ~4.1pp YoY — the H1 YoY gain is partly off a weak 2Q25 base, with 2Q26 cash cost ex-royalty/depreciation estimated at ~US$60.2/t (+9.2% QoQ).

G&A jumped 39.7% (others component to US$14,295k from US$7,477k); no explanation is disclosed — flagged as an open item (see §11.4 and internal_must_explain). External research (low confidence) suggests a step-up from 1Q26 rather than a 2Q26 event, possibly treasury-programme/transformation costs — treat as hypothesis only.

### 3.3 Net Finance Income/Expense and Other Income

- Finance income: US$18,046k (bank interest US$18,013k + other interest US$33k) vs US$20,569k in 6M25 — lower despite the rate environment, reflecting shrinking deposit balances (short-term deposits fell to US$66,442k from US$141,095k).
- Finance costs: US$3,719k vs US$5,501k (−32.4%), with loan interest nil (6M25: US$2,140k) consistent with the Rp320.2bn (US$17,931k) repayment of the Permata term loan during the half; residual costs are lease-related (Note 11: lease interest US$2,594k).
- Others, net: swung to −US$2,137k embedded net effect of an FX gain of US$6,414k (6M25: loss US$939k) offset by other losses of US$4,277k (6M25: US$1,644k). The fact-sheet caption records other_income_net of −US$4,277k. The composition (FX vs swap MTM vs disposals) is per Note 29 context: derivative liabilities rose to US$5,642k from US$278k at FYE25. The rupiah weakened ~6.1% over the half (average Rp17,196 vs Rp16,475), yet an FX gain was booked — the Note 33 swing of net Rupiah monetary position from net liabilities (US$20,335k) to net assets (US$6,906k) supports this; treat exact drivers as unresolved.

<addendum>
# Repository: IDX Financial Report Pipeline (`financial-report-llm`)

This project downloads financial reports from the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX),
converts them to markdown (docling), parses XLSX statements into DuckDB, and runs a
multi-stage LLM analysis pipeline that writes equity-research notes into the
`analysis/` Obsidian vault.

## Layout

- `scripts/report_pipeline/` — download → identify → collect → convert + XLSX parser
- `scripts/analysis_pipeline/` — 6-stage LLM analysis pipeline (needs `OPENCODE_API_KEY`)
- `scripts/notes_rag/rag.py` — hybrid BM25 + vector search over `analysis/`
- `idx_data/pipeline.duckdb` — pipeline state + financial data (source of truth)
- `idx_data/notes_rag.duckdb` — vault search index
- `raw/` identified PDFs · `results/` converted markdown · `analysis/` Obsidian vault

## Environment

- Python dependencies live in `.venv`; run scripts as `.venv/bin/python <script>` or
  `uv run <script>`.
- `duckdb` CLI is installed. Open the database read-only:
  `duckdb -readonly idx_data/pipeline.duckdb`.
- Model IDs and timeouts live in `config.yaml`; secrets (`OPENCODE_API_KEY`,
  `EXA_API_KEY`) in `.env` (gitignored — never commit or print).
- `.pi/settings.json` declares the project's pinned pi packages
  (`npm:pi-exa-search@0.1.3`, `npm:pi-web-access@0.41.0`) plus a delta entry
  that disables the global `npm:pi-web-search` extensions in this project.
  Project packages load after project trust (`--approve` for pipeline runs).
- Stage 3b (research) runs on pi with `exa_search` / `fetch_content`; Stage 4
  (writer) also runs on pi but with the read-only idx-tools `duckdb_query`,
  `notes_search`, `notes_fetch` plus `read`.
- `.pi/xdg/pi/web-search.json` configures `pi-web-access` for the Stage 3b
  research runner (fed via `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`); `.agents/skills/` holds dev-time
  Agent Skills (e.g. `build-with-exa`), not loaded by research runs.

## Conventions

- Quote financial values with their units, source table, and period.
  `financial_ratios` values are in billions of IDR (except `eps`);
  `xlsx_statements` values are raw IDR.
- Period formats: `financial_ratios.period` is `"YYYY-MM-DD"`; `xlsx_statements.period`
  and `pipeline_jobs.period` are lowercase `audit | tw1 | tw2 | tw3`.
- Prefer the notes vault (`notes_search`) and DuckDB (`duckdb_query`) over guessing.
  Cite the note path or the table you queried.
- Never commit runtime artifacts: `.env`, `idx_data/analysis/`, `.venv`, `idx_data/*.duckdb`.

## Project skills (`.pi/skills/`)

- `idx-financial-db` — query company ratios, balance sheet, income statement, cash flow
- `vault-search` — search the `analysis/` equity-research notes
- `report-review` — review/write an IDX equity analysis
- `data-pipelines` — run/inspect the report and analysis pipelines

</addendum>

# PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (ITMG) — Q2 2026
---

**Basis of preparation:** This analysis covers the six-month period ended 30 June 2026 ("6M26"), compared against the six months ended 30 June 2025 ("6M25") for income-statement and cash-flow items and against 31 December 2025 ("FYE25") for balance-sheet items. All figures are in **thousands of US Dollars** unless otherwise stated, drawn from the unaudited interim consolidated financial statements (source XLSX, authorised for issue 10 August 2026). Audited status: not stated for the interim (audited: null — treat as unaudited). Reported statement of cash flows and P&L are for the full six-month period; the quarter "Q2 2026" label reflects the interim filing cadence. Prior-period comparatives in the fact sheet for cash flow are 6M25. Reporting currency: USD; closing rate Rp17,856/US$ (30 Jun 2026) vs Rp16,782/US$ (31 Dec 2025); average rates Rp17,196 (6M26) vs Rp16,475 (6M25).

## 1. Executive Summary

ITMG delivered a solid first half: net revenue of US$1,000,491k (+8.8% YoY from US$919,416k), gross profit of US$256,477k (+14.1%), and net profit of US$109,514k (+16.5%), lifting net margin to 10.9% from 10.2%. Gross margin expanded ~2pp to 25.6% on an approximately +5% volume / +4% ASP mix (management-reported 12.3 Mt sold vs 11.7 Mt; ASP ~$81/t vs ~$78/t per ITMG's 6M26 news release, 10 Aug 2026), with own-coal sales up 11% while lower-margin third-party trading fell 20%. The external backdrop was supportive: high-kcal ESDM HBA benchmarks climbed through Q2 (US$123.91–131.85/t for 6,322 kcal/kg GAR across June–July periods) and Newcastle futures spiked to ~US$150/t in early June before easing, while Indonesia's RKAB quota cuts and DMO obligations tightened supply.

The balance sheet remains a fortress: cash of US$737,575k (plus US$66,442k short-term deposits per Note 9) against total bank debt of only US$18,360k net carrying value (Note 35 financing reconciliation), a current ratio of 3.46x, working capital of US$843,582k, and equity of US$1,910,488k (79.1% of assets). Two balance-sheet shifts deserve attention: restricted cash jumped 77% to US$85,787k, driven by the switch of mine reclamation/post-mining guarantees from bank guarantees to time deposits under Kepmen ESDM 344/2025 (all reclamation bank guarantees have been withdrawn and replaced with time deposits per the commitments note) — structurally "dead money"; and current prepaid taxes nearly doubled to US$55,677k as Indonesia's tax-refund (restitusi) pipeline slowed sharply (DJP refunds down ~33–38% YoY through 2026), a medium-confidence external explanation. The same refund slowdown is the primary driver of the 77.8% collapse in operating cash flow to US$62,376k (management: tax refund receipts ~US$169m lower YoY).

Capital returns are accelerating: 21,186,800 shares (1.9% of capital) repurchased in H1 for Rp464.5bn (US$26,571k), plus a further 10,690,300 shares (0.9%) in the subsequent-events window for Rp256.1bn (US$14,341k), under a mandate capped at Rp2,490bn; FY2025 dividends of US$114,584k (US$0.10/share full-year) were paid across the period. Annualized ROE of ~22.9% and ROA of ~18.2% on an exceptionally unlevered book make the earnings quality high even in a mediocre coal tape. No market data stub was provided, so valuation multiples are not computable here and are flagged as not available; the one comparable in the pipeline DB (ADRO, Oct-2025: P/E 5.65x, P/BV 0.62x, ROE 10.9%) suggests the sector continues to trade at deep-value multiples. Net thesis: a high-quality, net-cash thermal coal producer compounding shareholder returns through buybacks in a cyclical price environment with rising regulatory cash entanglement. The rating leans **HOLD/BUY on weakness** pending coal-price confirmation — see §14.

## 2. Revenue Analysis

### 2.1 Revenue Performance

| Metric | 6M26 (US$'000) | 6M25 (US$'000) | % Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Net revenue | 1,000,491 | 919,416 | +8.8% |
| Coal — third parties | 963,940 | 897,155 | +7.4% |
| Coal — related parties | 36,758 | 10,772 | +241% |
| Services | 1,626 | 2,257 | −28.0% |
| (Loss)/gain on coal swap | (1,833) | 9,232 | n.m. |

(Note 24 composition; percentages computed on the fact-sheet lines.) Revenue growth of 8.8% is volume- and price-led rather than trading-led. Related-party coal sales (Banpu entities, 3.67% of net revenue vs 1.17% in 6M25) rose sharply but remain immaterial to mix. The coal-swap line flipped from a US$9,232k gain to a US$1,833k loss, a ~US$11.1m earnings swing worth understanding: ITMG operates a volume-based swap programme (max 8,000,000 tonnes, tenors up to three years per Note 34) that flattens realised prices against index moves.

### 2.2 Revenue Drivers — Volume vs. Price

Per ITMG's own 6M26 news release (itmg.co.id, 10 Aug 2026 — external, management-disclosed figures): sales volume +5% to 12.3 Mt (11.7 Mt in 6M25) and ASP +4% to ~US$81/t (~US$78/t). Within that, own-coal sales rose 11% to 10.5 Mt while third-party trading fell 20% to 1.8 Mt — a favourable mix shift toward higher-margin own production. The same release flags production down 5% YoY to 9.9 Mt and a strip ratio of 10.3x (vs 9.3x), meaning the volume gain was partly inventory/trading-flow driven.

Price environment: ESDM HBA for 6,322 kcal/kg GAR printed US$123.91/t (period I June), US$126.58/t and US$131.85/t (periods I–II July 2026) per Bisnis.com (17 Jul 2026); Newcastle futures spiked to ~US$150/t in early June on Middle East conflict, then eased ~18% to a ~US$125–138/t range through July (CNBC Indonesia, 28 Jun 2026). Indonesia's 2026 RKAB quota cuts and DMO obligations constrained supply, supporting ASP. FX was a modest headwind on Rupiah cost translation (average Rp17,196 vs Rp16,475) but revenue is USD-denominated.

### 2.3 Revenue Composition Observations

Geographic mix (Note 34 / segment disclosures, 6M26 vs 6M25, US$'000): China 270,701 vs 243,211 (+11%); Japan 268,691 vs 203,860 (+32%); Philippines 104,432 vs 44,007 (+137%); Thailand 41,658 vs 10,772 (+287%); India 39,051 vs 115,100 (−66%); Domestic 174,660 vs 205,497 (−15%); Hong Kong 26,666 vs 23,071; Malaysia 21,886 vs 0 (new); Taiwan 16,712 vs 15,445; Vietnam 14,950 vs 0 (new); Bangladesh 14,423 vs 28,137 (−49%); Korea 6,661 vs 14,507 (−54%); Europe 0 vs 15,809. This matches the regional trade pattern: Asia's thermal imports rebounded (73.16 Mt in July, Reuters 28 Jul 2026) while India's seaborne thermal imports hit a four-year low on domestic output and renewables (Reuters, 18 Jun 2026). Customer concentration: three customers each owed >US$10,000k, equal to 43.65% of trade receivables (FYE25: four customers, 40.56%); Marubeni Corporation is disclosed as a >10%-of-net-revenue third-party customer in both periods (receivable balances US$135,384k at 30 Jun 2026 vs US$83,618k at 30 Jun 2025). Related-party receivables rose to 9% of trade receivables from 0%.

### 2.4 Revenue Sustainability and Forward Outlook

Key watch items: (1) post-period coal prices eased into a "lukewarm" tape by August (CNBC Indonesia, 2 Aug 2026) — H2 ASPs may not repeat Q2's spike; (2) Government Regulation No. 24/2026 (effective 1 June 2026) requires progressive channelling of coal, palm oil and ferro-alloy exports through BUMN Ekspor with a transition period ending 31 December 2026 — a structural change to export marketing not yet quantified by management; (3) MoEMR No. 6/2026 adds prior-approval requirements for coal blending and quarterly reporting — management assessed no material impact as at 30 June 2026; (4) DHE SDA rules (GR 8/2025, amended by 2/2026 and 21/2026) require export proceeds to sit in special accounts ≥12 months, with monthly conversion capped at 50% — already visible in the US$56,570k of DHE SDA special accounts and time deposits inside cash; (5) royalty audits at TCM for FY2018–2023 are in progress (letters received 12 May 2026). Reserve/runway: production and reserve tables were not disclosed in this chunk — cannot be stated. Permit runway is solid (BEK CCoW to 2041, TCM to 2035, JBG to 2035; see §7.2), but IMM's CCoW expires 31 March 2028, the nearest meaningful permit cliff.

External caution (Aldiracita 2Q26 flash, medium-high confidence): 2Q26 gross margin compressed ~2.1pp QoQ to ~24.6% even while up ~4.1pp YoY — the H1 YoY gain is partly off a weak 2Q25 base, with 2Q26 cash cost ex-royalty/depreciation estimated at ~US$60.2/t (+9.2% QoQ).
